title: "DGP Dossier: `r params$meta$dgp_id`"
output: html_document
params:
  meta: NULL
  dgp_id: "synth_heavytail"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
library(CausalStress)
library(ggplot2)
have_kableextra <- requireNamespace("kableExtra", quietly = TRUE)
if (requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) {
  patchwork_available <- TRUE
} else {
  patchwork_available <- FALSE
}
```

## 1. Identity & Status

```{r meta_table, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
stars <- params$meta$difficulty$stars %||% 0
active_star   <- '<span style="color: #f1c40f;">&#9733;</span>'
inactive_star <- '<span style="color: #e0e0e0;">&#9734;</span>'
difficulty_val <- paste0(
  strrep(active_star, max(0, stars)),
  strrep(inactive_star, max(0, 5 - stars)),
  " (", stars, "/5)"
)
prof <- params$meta$stress_profile

get_badge_color <- function(val) {
  val <- tolower(as.character(val))
  if (val %in% c("linear", "gaussian", "strong", "high", "easy", "stable", "att")) return("success")
  if (val %in% c("moderate", "medium", "experimental")) return("warning")
  if (val %in% c("nonlinear", "heavytail", "heavy", "poor", "severe", "deprecated", "heterogeneous")) return("danger")
  "secondary"
}

stress_val <- if (is.null(prof)) {
  "N/A"
} else {
  badge_vec <- mapply(
    function(k, v) {
      cls <- get_badge_color(v)
      sprintf('<span class="badge bg-%s" style="margin-right:4px;">%s: %s</span>', cls, k, v)
    },
    names(prof),
    unlist(prof),
    USE.NAMES = FALSE
  )
  paste0("&nbsp;", paste(badge_vec, collapse = ""))
}

status_raw <- params$meta$status %||% "N/A"
status_class <- get_badge_color(status_raw)
status_val <- sprintf('<span class="badge bg-%s">%s</span>', status_class, status_raw)

version_val <- params$meta$version %||% "N/A"
dgp_id_val <- params$meta$dgp_id %||% "N/A"
if (is.character(dgp_id_val)) {
  dgp_id_val <- dgp_id_val
}

meta_df <- tibble::tibble(
  Attribute = c("DGP ID", "Version", "Status", "Difficulty", "Stress Profile"),
  Value = c(
    dgp_id_val,
    version_val,
    status_val,
    difficulty_val,
    stress_val
  )
)

knitr::kable(meta_df, format = "html", col.names = NULL, escape = FALSE) %>%
  {
    if (have_kableextra) {
      kableExtra::kable_styling(
        .,
        bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed"),
        full_width = TRUE,
        position = "left"
      ) %>%
        kableExtra::column_spec(1, bold = TRUE, width = "150px")
    } else {
      .
    }
  }
```

## 2. What This DGP Stresses (Intent)

**Purpose:** Penalize estimators that rely on L2 loss under heavy-tailed noise.

This DGP is identical to the baseline linear design except for the outcome noise,
which is a Gaussian/Cauchy mixture. The Cauchy component makes the population mean
of observed outcomes undefined, so any estimator that minimizes squared error is
theoretically ill-posed and will suffer variance explosion.

This motivates quantile-based estimators (e.g., GenGC targeting medians) that are
well-defined under heavy tails.

## 3. Identification Assumptions (Explicit)

- Unconfoundedness holds by construction (treatment is assigned by a known
  propensity score).
- Overlap is moderate (`p(X)` bounded away from 0 and 1 for most of the mass).
- Structural ATT is defined as the mean of the signal `tau(X)` on treated units
  (Constitution Article I), independent of realized noise.

## 4. Mathematical Specification

### Covariates
\[
X \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_5)
\]

### Propensity
\[
p(X) = \text{expit}(0.5 X_1 - 0.5 X_2)
\]

### Baseline Outcome and Treatment Effect
\[
\mu_0(X) = 1 + X_1 + 0.5 X_2
\]
\[
\tau(X) = 1 + 0.5 X_1
\]

### Noise Mixture (Heavy Tails)
\[
\varepsilon \sim 0.8 \cdot \mathcal{N}(0, 0.5) + 0.2 \cdot \text{Cauchy}(0, 1)
\]

**Moment note:** The Cauchy component has undefined mean and variance. Therefore the
population mean of realized outcomes is undefined, and any L2/MSE estimator is not
well-posed in the population.

### Potential Outcomes
\[
Y_0 = \mu_0(X) + \varepsilon_0,\quad
Y_1 = \mu_0(X) + \tau(X) + \varepsilon_1
\]

## 5. Oracle Truth Definition

- **ATT (Structural):** \(\mathbb{E}[\tau(X) \mid W=1]\), computed from the
  deterministic signal \(\tau(X)\). This is well-defined even when \(\mathbb{E}[Y]\)
  is not.
- **QST (Distributional):** computed on the canonical tau grid via oracle Monte Carlo
  as specified in `cs_get_oracle_qst()`.

## 6. Visual Diagnostics (n = 5000)

```{r visuals, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
set.seed(123)
dgp <- dgp_synth_heavytail(n = 5000, seed = 123)
df <- dgp$df

p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = p, fill = factor(w))) +
  geom_histogram(alpha = 0.6, bins = 30, position = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Propensity Distribution (Moderate Overlap)",
       x = "p(X)", y = "Count", fill = "W") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = X1, y = structural_te)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(title = expression(paste("Treatment Effect: ", tau(X), " = 1 + 0.5Â·X1")),
       x = "X1", y = "structural_te") +
  theme_minimal()

p3 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = X1, y = X2, color = factor(w))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "Covariate Balance", x = "X1", y = "X2", color = "W") +
  theme_minimal()

p4 <- ggplot(dgp$true_qst, aes(x = tau, y = value)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = dgp$true_att, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray70") +
  geom_line(color = "#2c3e50", size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "True Quantile Shift (QST)",
    subtitle = "Solid line: True effect at each quantile | Dashed: Mean ATT",
    x = "Quantile (tau)",
    y = "Treatment Effect"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

if (patchwork_available) {
  library(patchwork)
  (p1 + p2) / (p3 + p4)
} else {
  print(p1)
  print(p2)
  print(p3)
  print(p4)
}
```

## 7. Empirical Validation

We run light validation with `n = 1000` and `seeds = 1:20`. The goal is to show
variance explosion for OLS under L2 loss. We do **not** run GenGC here to keep
doc builds fast.

```{r empirical, cache=TRUE}
run_fast <- function(est_id) {
  cs_run_seeds(
    dgp_id        = "synth_heavytail",
    estimator_id  = est_id,
    n             = 1000,
    seeds         = 1:20,
    bootstrap     = FALSE,
    parallel      = FALSE,
    show_progress = FALSE,
    config        = list(ci_method = "none")
  )
}

res_lm     <- run_fast("lm_att")
res_oracle <- run_fast("oracle_att")

summary_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(res_lm, res_oracle) %>%
  cs_tidy() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(estimator_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_bias = mean(att_error, na.rm = TRUE),
    rmse      = sqrt(mean(att_error^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(summary_tbl, digits = 3, caption = "Empirical validation (n=1000, seeds=1:20)")
```

**Interpretation:** OLS fails not because it is biased in the limit, but because
its variance is infinite under a Cauchy mixture. The RMSE will fluctuate wildly
across seeds (typical values ~8.0 in quick runs). The oracle estimator remains
stable, confirming the truth layer.

## 8. Failure Mode Summary

- **L2-based estimators (OLS/IPW with mean targets):** variance explosion; unstable RMSE.
- **Quantile-based estimators:** well-defined under heavy tails (motivation for GenGC).

## 9. Implementation Reference

- Generator: `R/dgp-synth-heavytail.R`
- Oracle truth: `cs_get_oracle_qst("synth_heavytail", version = "1.3.0")`
- Metadata: `inst/dgp_meta/synth_heavytail.yml`

## 10. Validation Checklist

- [x] Mixture noise matches spec (0.8 * Normal + 0.2 * Cauchy).
- [x] Structural ATT defined on `tau(X)` (signal-only).
- [x] Visual diagnostics show extreme tails.
- [x] OLS variance explosion demonstrated.
- [x] Oracle estimator stable across seeds.
